speaker: Otis
text: Senator Kerry, after talking with several co-workers and family and friends, I asked the ones who said they were not voting for you, “Why?” They said that you were too wishy-washy.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Yes, I certainly do.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, a minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Charlie, thank you, and thank our panelists.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, I would follow up, but we have a series of questions on Iraq, and so I will turn to the next questioner.

speaker: Dahle
text: Mr. President, yesterday in a statement you admitted that Iraq did not have weapons of mass destruction, but justified the invasion by stating, I quote, “He retained the knowledge, the materials, the means and the intent to produce weapons of mass destruction and could have passed this knowledge to our terrorist enemies.”

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Each situation is different, Robin.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Robin, I’m going to answer your question.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, I do want to follow up on this one, because there were several questions from the audience along this line.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: (OFF-MIKE)

speaker: Gibson
text: Go ahead. Go ahead.

speaker: Gibson
text: Well, I was going to have you do the rebuttal on it, but you go ahead.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You remember the last debate?

speaker: John Kerry
text: The goal of the sanctions was not to remove Saddam Hussein, it was to remove the weapons of mass destruction. And, Mr. President, just yesterday the Duelfer report told you and the whole world they worked. He didn’t have weapons of mass destruction, Mr. President. That was the objective.

speaker: Gibson
text: We’re going to have another question now on the subject of Iraq.

speaker: Baldi
text: Senator Kerry, the U.S. is preparing a new Iraq government and will proceed to withdraw U.S. troops.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Anthony, I would not. I have laid out a different plan, because the president’s plan is not working. You see that every night on television.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Two days ago in the Oval Office, I met with the finance minister from Iraq. He came to see me. And he talked about how optimistic he was and the country was about heading toward elections.

speaker: Gibson
text: Do you want to follow up, Senator?

speaker: John Kerry
text: Yes, sir, please.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: First of all, we didn’t find out he didn’t have weapons until we got there, and my opponent thought he had weapons and told everybody he thought he had weapons.

speaker: Gibson
text: The next question is for President Bush, and it comes from Nikki Washington.

speaker: Washington
text: Thank you.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: No, I appreciate that. I — listen, I — we’ve got a great country. I love our values. And I recognize I’ve made some decisions that have caused people to not understand the great values of our country.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Nikki, that’s a question that’s been raised by a lot of people around the country.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I remember sitting in the White House looking at those generals, saying, “Do you have what you need in this war? Do you have what it takes?”

speaker: John Kerry
text: You rely on good military people to execute the military component of the strategy, but winning the peace is larger than just the military component.

speaker: Gibson
text: The next question is for Senator Kerry, and it comes from over here, from Randee Jacobs.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Is it Randee?

speaker: Jacobs
text: Yes, Randee.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I don’t think you can just rely on U.N. sanctions, Randee. But you’re absolutely correct, it is a threat, it’s a huge threat.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, a minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That answer almost made me want to scowl.

speaker: Gibson
text: We’re going to move on, Mr. President, with a question for you. And it comes from Daniel Farley.

speaker: Farley
text: Mr. President, since we continue to police the world, how do you intend to maintain our military presence without reinstituting a draft?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Yes, that’s a great question. Thanks.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Daniel, I don’t support a draft.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, let’s extend for a minute…

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me just — I’ve got to answer this.

speaker: Gibson
text: Exactly. And with Reservists being held on duty…

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me answer what he just said, about around the world.

speaker: Gibson
text: Well, I want to get into the issue of the back-door draft…

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You tell Tony Blair we’re going alone. Tell Tony Blair we’re going alone. Tell Silvio Berlusconi we’re going alone. Tell Aleksander Kwasniewski of Poland we’re going alone.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Mr. President, countries are leaving the coalition, not joining. Eight countries have left it.

speaker: Gibson
text: The next question, Senator Kerry, is for you, and it comes from Ann Bronsing, who I believe is over in this area.

speaker: Bronsing
text: Senator Kerry, we have been fortunate that there have been no further terrorist attacks on American soil since 9/11. Why do you think this is?

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you very much, Ann.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: That’s an odd thing to say, since we’ve tripled the homeland security budget from $10 billion to $30 billion.

speaker: Gibson
text: I want to extend for a minute, Senator. And I’m curious about something you said. You said, “It’s not when, but if.” You think it’s inevitable because the sense of security is a very basic thing with everybody in this country worried about their kids.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, the president and his experts have told America that it’s not a question of if; it’s a question of when. And I accept what the president has said. These terrorists are serious, they’re deadly, and they know nothing except trying to kill.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, we’ll talk about the tax cut for middle class here in a minute. But yes, I’m worried. I’m worried. I’m worried about our country. And all I can tell you is every day I know that there’s people working overtime, doing the very best they can. And the reason I’m worried is because there’s a vicious enemy that has an ideology of hate.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, we’re going to turn to questions now on domestic policy. And we’re going to start with health issues.

speaker: Horstman
text: Mr. President, why did you block the reimportation of safer and inexpensive drugs from Canada which would have cut 40 to 60 percent off of the cost?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I haven’t yet. Just want to make sure they’re safe. When a drug comes in from Canada, I want to make sure it cures you and doesn’t kill you.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: John, you heard the president just say that he thought he might try to be for it.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: If they’re safe, they’re coming. I want to remind you that it wasn’t just my administration that made the decision on safety. President Clinton did the same thing, because we have an obligation to protect you.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Actually, Mr. President, in 1997 we fixed Medicare, and I was one of the people involved in it.

speaker: Gibson
text: The next question is for Senator Kerry. And this comes from Norma-Jean Laurent.

speaker: Laurent
text: Senator Kerry, you’ve stated your concern for the rising cost of health care, yet you chose a vice presidential candidate who has made millions of dollars successfully suing medical professionals. How do you reconcile this with the voters?

speaker: John Kerry
text: Very easily. John Edwards is the author of the Patients’ Bill of Rights. He wanted to give people rights. John Edwards and I support tort reform. We both believe that, as lawyers — I’m a lawyer, too. And I believe that we will be able to get a fix that has alluded everybody else because we know how to do it.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, a minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me see where to start here.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, we got several questions along this line, and I’m just curious if you’d go further on what you talked about with tort reform. Would you be favoring capping awards on pain and suffering? Would you limit attorney’s fees?

speaker: John Kerry
text: A follow-up…

speaker: Gibson
text: Yes. A follow-up on this for…

speaker: John Kerry
text: Yes, I think we should look at the punitive and we should have some limitations.

speaker: Gibson
text: We’ll get to that in just a minute.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: You’re right, what does matter is a plan. He said he’s for — you’re now for capping punitive damages?

speaker: Gibson
text: The next question is for President Bush, and it comes from Matthew O’Brien.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Right, thank you for that.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Let me begin by saying that my health-care plan is not what the president described. It is not a government takeover.

speaker: Gibson
text: I both — I heard you both say — I have heard you both say during the campaign, I just heard you say it, that you’re going to cut the deficit by a half in four years. But I didn’t hear one thing in the last three and a half minutes that would indicate how either one of you do that.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, look at the budget. One is make sure Congress doesn’t overspend.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, 30 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: After 9/11, after the recession had ended, the president asked for another tax cut and promised 5.6 million jobs would be created. He lost 1.6 million, ladies and gentlemen. And most of that tax cut went to the wealthiest people in the country.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, the next question will be for you, and it comes from James Varner, who I believe is in this section.

speaker: Varner
text: Thank you.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Absolutely. Yes. Right into the camera. Yes. I am not going to raise taxes.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, 90 seconds.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: He’s just not credible when he talks about being fiscally conservative. He’s just not credible. If you look at his record in the Senate, he voted to break the caps — the spending caps — over 200 times.

speaker: Gibson
text: No, you can keep going.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Good. You looked at me like my clock was up.

speaker: Gibson
text: I’m going to come back one more time to how these numbers add up and how you can cut that deficit in half in four years, given what you’ve both said.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, first of all, the president’s figures of $2.2 trillion just aren’t accurate. Those are the fuzzy math figures put together by some group that works for the campaign. That’s not the number.

speaker: Gibson
text: Thirty seconds. I’m sorry, thirty seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Yes, I mean, he’s got a record. It’s been there for 20 years. You can run, but you can’t hide. He voted 98 times to raise taxes. I mean, these aren’t make-up figures.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, the next question is for you, and it comes from James Hubb over here.

speaker: Hubb
text: Mr. President, how would you rate yourself as an environmentalist? What specifically has your administration done to improve the condition of our nation’s air and water supply?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Off-road diesel engines — we have reached an agreement to reduce pollution from off-road diesel engines by 90 percent.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Boy, to listen to that — the president, I don’t think, is living in a world of reality with respect to the environment.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, had we joined the Kyoto treaty, which I guess he’s referring to, it would have cost America a lot of jobs.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, 30 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: The fact is that the Kyoto treaty was flawed. I was in Kyoto, and I was part of that. I know what happened. But this president didn’t try to fix it. He just declared it dead, ladies and gentlemen, and we walked away from the work of 160 nations over 10 years.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, the next question is for you. It involves jobs, which is a topic of the news today.

speaker: Barrow
text: Senator Kerry, how can the U.S. be competitive in manufacturing given — in manufacturing, excuse me — given the wage necessary and comfortably accepted for American workers to maintain the standard of living that they expect?

speaker: John Kerry
text: Jane, there are a lot of ways to be competitive. And unfortunately again I regret this administration has not seized them and embraced them. Let me give you an example.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me start with how to control the cost of health care: medical liability reform, for starters, which he’s opposed.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator, I want to extend for a minute, you talk about tax credits to stop outsourcing. But when you have IBM documents that I saw recently where you can hire a programmer for $12 in China, $56 an hour here, tax credits won’t cut it.

speaker: John Kerry
text: You can’t stop all outsourcing, Charlie. I’ve never promised that. I’m not going to, because that would be pandering. You can’t.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I own a timber company?

speaker: Gibson
text: President Bush, the next question is for you, and it comes from Rob Fowler, who I believe is over in this area.

speaker: Fowler
text: President Bush, 45 days after 9/11, Congress passed the Patriot Act, which takes away checks on law enforcement and weakens American citizens’ rights and freedoms, especially Fourth Amendment rights.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I appreciate that.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Former Governor Racicot, as chairman of the Republican Party, said he thought that the Patriot Act has to be changed and fixed.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, the next question is for you, and it comes from Elizabeth Long.

speaker: Long
text: Senator Kerry, thousands of people have already been cured or treated by the use of adult stem cells or umbilical cord stem cells. However, no one has been cured by using embryonic stem cells.

speaker: John Kerry
text: You know, Elizabeth, I really respect your — the feeling that’s in your question. I understand it. I know the morality that’s prompting that question, and I respect it enormously.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, a minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Embryonic stem-cell research requires the destruction of life to create a stem cell. I’m the first president ever to allow funding — federal funding — for embryonic stem-cell research. I did to because I too hope that we’ll discover cures from the stem cells and from the research derived.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator, 30 seconds, less extent.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, you talk about walking a waffle line — he says he’s allowed it, which means he’s going to allow the destruction of life up to a certain amount and then he isn’t going to allow it.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Let me make sure you understand my decision. Those stem- cells lines already existed. The embryo had already been destroyed prior to my decision.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, the next question is for you, and it comes from Jonathan Michaelson, over here.

speaker: Michaelson
text: Mr. President, if there were a vacancy in the Supreme Court and you had the opportunity to fill that position today, who would you choose and why?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I’m not telling.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you, Charlie.

speaker: Gibson
text: Going to go to the final two questions now, and the first one will be for Senator Kerry. And this comes from Sarah Degenhart.

speaker: Degenhart
text: Senator Kerry, suppose you are speaking with a voter who believed abortion is murder and the voter asked for reassurance that his or her tax dollars would not go to support abortion, what would you say to that person?

speaker: John Kerry
text: I would say to that person exactly what I will say to you right now.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, minute and a half.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I’m trying to decipher that.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator, do you want to follow up? Thirty seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Well, again, the president just said, categorically, my opponent is against this, my opponent is against that. You know, it’s just not that simple. No, I’m not.

speaker: Gibson
text: And 30 seconds, Mr. President.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Well, it’s pretty simple when they say: Are you for a ban on partial birth abortion? Yes or no?

speaker: Gibson
text: And the final question of the evening will be addressed to President Bush and it will come from Linda Grabel. Linda Grabel’s over here.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Put a head fake on us.

speaker: Gibson
text: I got faked out myself.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Hi, Linda.

speaker: Grabel
text: President Bush, during the last four years, you have made thousands of decisions that have affected millions of lives. Please give three instances in which you came to realize you had made a wrong decision, and what you did to correct it. Thank you.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: I have made a lot of decisions, and some of them little, like appointments to boards you never heard of, and some of them big.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: But history will look back, and I’m fully prepared to accept any mistakes that history judges to my administration, because the president makes the decisions, the president has to take the responsibility.

speaker: Gibson
text: Senator Kerry, a minute and a half.

speaker: John Kerry
text: I believe the president made a huge mistake, a catastrophic mistake, not to live up to his own standard, which was: build a true global coalition, give the inspectors time to finish their job and go through the U.N. process to its end and go to war as a last resort.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: He complains about the fact our troops don’t have adequate equipment, yet he voted against the $87 billion supplemental I sent to the Congress and then issued one of the most amazing quotes in political history: “I actually did vote for the $87 billion before I voted against it.”

speaker: Gibson
text: And, Senator Kerry, 30 seconds.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Not necessarily be in power, but here’s what I’ll say about the $87 billion.

speaker: Gibson
text: That’s going to conclude the questioning. We’re going to go now to closing statements, two minutes from each candidate.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Do you want to go first?

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Either way.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you.

speaker: John Kerry
text: Thank you, all of you, for taking part.

speaker: George H.W. Bush
text: Charlie, thanks.

speaker: Gibson
text: Mr. President, Senator Kerry, that concludes tonight’s debate.
